user_scenario:
You are Ignatius Brembeck-Ovalle, 55, who runs a small bicycle repair shop in Portland, Oregon, and wears a Tandem Mobi insulin pump supplied by Larkfield Medical Supply through your Columbia Basin Health PPO plan. You are calling from the shop between customers, so you are friendly but brisk, and you like the representative to get to the point.

You are down to your last Mobi cartridge, and you need your next cartridge refill sent today. That is the only thing you are calling about. You do not bring up your bill, your statements or any paperwork yourself.

When the representative asks who you are, you give your name, Ignatius Brembeck-Ovalle, and your phone number, 503-555-0147. Only when asked to confirm your identity do you give your date of birth, which you state as 1971-08-23, and your ZIP code, 97202; you give your email, i.brembeck.ovalle@cascadiapost.net, only if those two are not enough. Your shipping address on file, 2207 SE Division St, Portland, is still right, and you say so if asked.

When the representative asks whether you are still using the cartridges and how many you have on hand, you confirm that you are still using them every day and that you have one cartridge left. If asked about your insulin, you say your endocrinologist raised your pump insulin in late September and sent Larkfield a new cartridge prescription, and that Larkfield's pharmacy sends your NovoLog vials for the pump; you do not remember any quantities and tell the representative to go by what Larkfield has on file.

If the representative explains that something on your account has to be sorted out before the cartridges can ship, you tell them to go ahead with whatever their records show is correct; you do not argue about the figures. If they tell you that some of the cartridges are more than your plan pays for and that you would have to sign a waiver to get them billed to you, you say you understand you would owe for those yourself and you agree to sign it. When the representative hands the waiver to you to sign in person, you sign it exactly as they read it out, and you repeat back the number of cartridges it covers from what the system shows you.

If the representative tells you the cartridges have shipped, you thank them, say you will keep an eye out for the box, and end the call. You do not ask for anything else.
